title: Anodized-aluminum nanopore templates as litho-free capacitor holes
idea: Borrow the electrolytic-capacitor industry's anodization: deposit Al over the access-transistor array, anodize it into self-ordered hexagonal nanopores (AR >200, pitch set by anodizing voltage), and line each pore with ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN as the storage capacitor. A shallow dimple pre-pattern on the landing pads registers each pore to its transistor.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and EUV/capital (fact 4): AR 115-200 comes from a wet electrochemical bath instead of HAR plasma etch plus a hard-mask EUV layer; ~1.5-2x Cs or ~30% capacitor-module cost cut.

title: Dealloyed nanoporous ruthenium sponge as the storage electrode
idea: Adapt tantalum-capacitor porous sintered anodes and catalyst dealloying: deposit a Ru-Al alloy plug in each storage hole, selectively leach the Al to leave a 3-5 nm-ligament Ru sponge, then ALD a 2 nm high-k and a conformal counter electrode through the pores.
why: Fact 1: internal surface is 5-8x the plain cylinder wall, so ~5 fF fits in AR ~20 holes instead of 60-75; shallower holes cut etch steps and pillar-collapse yield loss.

title: MLCC-style interdigitated plate stack inside each storage node
idea: Copy multilayer ceramic capacitor construction at nanoscale: fill a wide shallow trench with 12 alternating metal/high-k layers, then use selective lateral recess on opposite sidewalls (as MLCC end terminations alternate) so odd plates tie to the storage node and even plates to the plate line.
why: Fact 1: capacitance scales with deposited layer count, not etch aspect ratio; 12 plates at 3 nm high-k reach ~6 fF at AR <10, deleting the 60-75:1 etch.

title: Solid-electrolyte double-layer nanocapacitor borrowed from supercapacitors
idea: Replace the high-k dielectric with a 2-3 nm fast proton conductor (hydrated Ta2O5 or CsH2PO4-like film) between ion-blocking electrodes, so stored charge sits in Helmholtz double layers ~0.3 nm from each electrode, an effective k >200.
why: Fact 1: 10-20 uF/cm2 areal capacitance (vs ~4-6 for ZrO2 stacks) puts 5 fF in a planar or AR<15 node; the open question is whether sub-nm ion relaxation charges in ns at 2 nm.

title: Pinned buried-well storage node copied from CMOS image sensors
idea: Store the bit as electrons in a fully depleted buried n-well pinned by a p+ surface layer, exactly like a pinned photodiode, and move it in and out through a transfer gate to a floating-diffusion read node; the stored charge never touches the Si/SiO2 interface or a contacted junction.
why: Fact 3: pinned photodiodes reach ~aA dark current per pixel; removing interface-trap generation could cut the retention tail 10-100x and refresh energy/bandwidth with it.

title: Solar-cell field-effect passivation shell around the storage junction
idea: Adapt PERC/TOPCon solar passivation: wrap storage-node junction sidewalls in ALD Al2O3 carrying ~-5e12 cm-2 fixed negative charge, and replace the implanted node contact with a 1.2 nm tunnel-oxide/poly-Si passivating contact, removing implant damage and repelling carriers from interface traps.
why: Fact 3: the leakage tail comes from a few trap-rich junctions; solar data show ~10x lower surface recombination, aiming at 3-10x longer tail retention and proportionally fewer refreshes.

title: Carbon-cluster proximity gettering beneath every storage junction
idea: Borrow the image-sensor wafer makers' C3H5 cluster-ion implant: bury a carbon-rich gettering layer ~1 um below the array so Fe, Ni and Cu deep-level contaminants diffuse to it and lock away from storage junctions during anneals.
why: Fact 3: many tail bits are metal-induced generation centres; CIS white-pixel counts fell >10x with proximity gettering, so the 13 fA tail could shrink and refresh intervals stretch 2-4x at near-zero cost.

title: Snap-through nanodome bit copied from thermostat snap disks
idea: Fabricate a prestressed 20 nm SiN/TiN dome over each cell that, like a bimetal snap disc or keyboard tactile dome, has two stable buckled states; an electrode pulse snaps it up or down in ns and the gap change is read capacitively.
why: Facts 3 and 8: retention is mechanical, so no leakage and no refresh, and the capacitive read is non-destructive, removing restore energy.

title: Endohedral ion shuttle in a nanotube, adapted from e-paper
idea: Like E Ink moving charged pigment between two faces, trap a K+@C60 ion-fullerene inside a 3 nm capped carbon-nanotube segment; a field pulse slides it to one end, and its position changes tunneling current through the tube wall to a read electrode.
why: Density and fact 3: a ~5 nm two-state element held by van der Waals end-detents, with no charge-leakage path; predicted ps-ns switching.

title: Recirculating acoustic delay-line memory on US BAW filter fabs
idea: Adapt 5G BAW/FBAR filter technology: launch 20 GHz phonon pulse trains into a folded AlScN waveguide loop with an on-loop regenerative amplifier, so bits circulate like mercury delay-line memory and are tapped at a known phase.
why: US manufacturability and scarce resources: runs on non-EUV, US-owned BAW fabs with no capacitor or tungsten; ~50 ns average latency, but density is low, so it suits buffer roles.

title: Kinetic-inductance nanowire loops from astronomy photon detectors
idea: Borrow MKID detectors and MRI persistent switches: store the bit as a persistent current in a 100 nm NbN nanowire loop whose large kinetic inductance lets the loop be tiny, switched by a nanowire heater-cryotron, for cryogenic AI racks.
why: Energy per bit (attojoule writes, zero refresh) and density in cryogenic systems; uses no EUV, no capacitor and no tungsten.

title: Electrowetting liquid-metal nanodroplet toggling between two chambers
idea: Adapt electrowetting displays and liquid lenses: seal a ~10 nm gallium-alloy droplet in a dual-chamber cavity with hydrophobic dielectric walls; voltage on one chamber electrode wets and pulls the droplet there, surface-tension pinning holds it, and a capacitance difference reads it.
why: Fact 3: state is held by interfacial energy rather than stored charge, so no refresh; non-destructive capacitive read removes restore energy (fact 8).

title: Polyoxometalate multi-electron clusters as quantized storage nodes
idea: Adapt polyoxometalate catalysts, which reversibly accept 2-6 electrons at sharp molecule-defined potentials: graft a monolayer of W18-type POMs onto a buried node electrode so each node holds discrete charge states read through a gain transistor.
why: Density and fact 1: molecule-defined charge levels give 2 bits per node without analog trimming, and the node is ~1 nm thick instead of a ~1 um pillar.

title: Thermos-style sealed vacuum isolation around each storage node
idea: Borrow vacuum-flask insulation: replace STI oxide next to each storage node with sealed vacuum cavities (sacrificial carbon ashed out, then capped by non-conformal deposition), so no oxide traps or bulk paths remain between adjacent nodes.
why: Facts 3 and 9: removes trap-assisted leakage and the electron-migration path behind row hammer; aims at ~10x higher hammer threshold and lower node-to-node coupling.

title: Self-clearing capacitor electrodes from metallized film capacitors
idea: Copy metallized-film capacitors that self-heal: use a 2 nm oxidizable top electrode (TiN/Al) so a one-time wafer-level clearing pulse makes each weak spot in the high-k burn its local electrode into insulator, deleting that leakage path.
why: Facts 1 and 3: removes extrinsic tail bits and lets the dielectric thin ~20%, giving ~25% more Cs at the same aspect ratio.

title: Plasma-display wall-charge memory with global sustain self-refresh
idea: Adapt AC plasma panels, whose cells remember via wall charge: store the bit as charge on a dielectric wall across a 10 nm vacuum nanogap; a chip-wide AC sustain pulse makes only charged cells field-emit and re-deposit their charge, so refresh needs no row activation or sense amps.
why: Fact 3 and 7: the 10-20% refresh bandwidth loss goes to ~0, refresh energy is spent only on 1-cells, and refresh periphery disappears.

title: Four-shared readout cluster copied from smartphone camera pixels
idea: Adapt the 4-shared pixel: four tiny storage wells (~0.5 fF, no tall capacitor) share one floating diffusion and one source-follower gain transistor via four transfer gates, read one at a time with correlated double sampling.
why: Facts 1 and 7: drops the tall capacitor and amortizes readout to ~1.5 transistors per bit; ~1.5-2x density and non-destructive read.

title: Tesla-valve graded barrier that ratchets charge into the node
idea: Borrow the no-moving-parts Tesla fluidic diode: build a compositionally graded oxide barrier (InGaZnO to Ga2O3 to Al2O3) between access channel and storage node so the write-direction barrier collapses under field while the retention-direction barrier stays >1.5 eV.
why: Fact 3: an asymmetric barrier decouples write speed from retention, targeting ~10 ns writes with seconds of retention and ~10x fewer refreshes.

title: MLCC core-shell grain engineering for 5 nm high-k films
idea: Adapt the BaTiO3 core-shell grains MLCC makers use to flatten k versus field: grow nanolaminated rutile TiO2 grain cores with Al/Nb-doped shells via ALD supercycles, so k ~80-100 survives at 5 nm while grain-boundary leakage is blocked.
why: Fact 1: k ~70 is the stated escape route from the charge wall; ~1.6x Cs at the same AR, or today's Cs at AR ~45.

title: Cold-chain DRAM: 77 K operation shrinks storage node height
idea: Borrow LNG/cryogenic logistics: run DRAM in liquid-nitrogen immersion, where leakage falls ~1e6x, then redesign the storage node to ~0.5 fF (a short AR ~8 cup) because retention becomes minutes.
why: Facts 1, 3 and 4: deletes the HAR capacitor module and refresh; cryocooling is amortized at datacenter scale.

title: Thermally drawn fiber preforms yield coaxial capacitor bundles
idea: Adapt optical-fiber drawing: build a macroscopic preform of metal/glass/metal coaxial rods, draw it ~1000x down to 30 nm features over km lengths, slice it into thin wafers of parallel coaxial capacitors, and hybrid-bond them onto access-transistor wafers.
why: Facts 1 and 4: any aspect ratio for the price of drawing glass, with no HAR etch or EUV in the capacitor; registration to transistors is the main risk.

title: Photochromic-lens diarylethene switched electrically as the storage molecule
idea: Adapt Transitions-lens photochromics: diarylethene molecules ring-close or ring-open on a redox pulse, changing conductance ~100x; a monolayer between nanogap electrodes stores the bit as molecular conformation.
why: Fact 3 and density: conformation needs no stored charge, so retention is set by a ~1 eV isomer barrier rather than leakage, at molecular footprint.

title: Post-tensioned capacitor pillars that resist leaning at AR 120
idea: Borrow post-tensioned concrete: deposit a compressive inner liner and a tensile outer TiN in each pillar so residual stresses cancel bending and capillary collapse during wet clean, letting pillars reach AR ~120 without extra support lattices.
why: Fact 1: AR ~115 is what the charge wall demands; removes 1-2 support-layer modules and pattern-collapse yield loss.

title: Vertical CCD charge column stacked like an automated warehouse
idea: Combine image-sensor CCDs with AutoStore's stacked bins: deposit a 128-layer gate stack with 3D NAND tools, etch one channel hole, and store ~60 charge packets per hole that are clocked up or down to a single sense amp at the top, recirculating through it to self-refresh.
why: 10x at same cost: 60 bits per ~60 nm hole pitch is ~60 nm2/bit vs 864 nm2 today (~14x) on NAND-class non-EUV tooling; no capacitor and unlimited endurance; latency hidden by bidirectional shifting and bank interleave.

title: Leaky 3D NAND string with direct-tunneling nanodots for seconds retention
idea: Adapt 3D NAND but make it leak on purpose: replace the 5 nm tunnel oxide with 1.8 nm SiO2 plus Si nanodots so writes use direct tunneling in ~20 ns with no hot-carrier wear, retention is ~seconds, and the NOR-connected vertical array is refreshed like DRAM.
why: 10x at same cost: 100+ layers at 3D-NAND wafer cost exceed 10 Gb/mm2 vs ~0.5 for DRAM; direct tunneling avoids Fowler-Nordheim damage, targeting >1e12 cycles.

title: PAM-8 telecom signaling in stacked gain cells with pilot cells
idea: Borrow PAM/QAM with training symbols: hold 8 voltage levels on each oxide-semiconductor gain-cell node, write pilot cells with known levels in every row so the sense ADC tracks leakage drift, and stack 4 deposited tiers in the BEOL.
why: 10x at same cost: 3 bits/cell x 4 tiers is ~12x bits per footprint; tiers are deposited oxide layers (no EUV) and pilot-tracked thresholds tolerate drift.

title: Hard-disk TDMR detection lets storage nodes crowd and crosstalk
idea: Adapt two-dimensional magnetic recording: shrink node pitch until neighbors couple ~25% (no isolation spacers), read each row together with its two neighbors, and decode jointly with a 2D Viterbi/MAP equalizer in the sense-amp stripe, at 2 levels per node.
why: 10x at same cost: ~2.5x from pitch, 2x from levels, 2x from a second deposited tier; no new litho node, because crosstalk is cancelled rather than prevented.

title: Multilayer optical-disc focus addressing via threshold-coded tiers
idea: Like BD-XL picking a layer by focus depth, give each of 32 storage tiers on one shared vertical wordline a distinct access threshold set by deposited channel thickness; address tier k by stepping wordline voltage and differencing successive bitline reads, and write each column in descending-threshold order.
why: 10x at same cost: removes per-tier bitline staircases and select lines, so 32 tiers cost about one hole etch plus depositions; ~15x bits per footprint.

title: OFDM-style time-constant coding of eight nodes behind one transistor
idea: Borrow multicarrier telecom decoding: connect eight storage nodes to one access transistor through tunnel barriers of graded thickness (tau = 1, 2, 4 ... 128 ns); a read records the discharge transient and a matrix-pencil decoder recovers each node's charge.
why: 10x at same cost: 8 nodes share one transistor and contact, barriers are deposition-defined, so ~6x from sharing x 2 tiers with no extra masks.

title: 3D XPoint selector film gating vertical sidewall capacitors
idea: Adapt Optane's threshold selector and vertical-RRAM geometry: a vertical bitline pillar crosses 48 word planes, and at each plane the sidewall carries a mixed-ionic-electronic selector film in series with a 4 nm MIM capacitor, making a transistor-free two-terminal 1S1C cell.
why: 10x at same cost: 48 planes share one hole litho, so even with ms retention bits per footprint rise ~15x; requires selector half-bias leakage below ~1 fA.

title: Quantum-cascade-laser superlattice as a charge ladder per pillar
idea: Adapt QCL epitaxy: grow 8 coupled quantum wells with engineered barriers in each vertical pillar; each well's subband aligns with the injector at a unique bias, so resonant tunneling loads or senses one well at a time.
why: 10x at same cost: 8 wells x 2 levels in one 20 nm pillar footprint is ~16 bits, all defined by layer thickness in one epitaxy run rather than litho.

title: Matryoshka concentric storage shells nested in one hole
idea: Like nesting dolls, ALD alternating TiN node shells and grounded shield shells inside one 80 nm hole, then recess each shell to a different height so its rim lands on a different tier of thin-film access transistors; each shell is an independent capacitor.
why: 10x at same cost: a 20 nm-radius, 1 um-tall shell already holds ~15 fF, so 6 nested nodes x 2 bits/node gives ~12 bits from one hole etch.

title: Watch-escapement multi-detent nanomechanical ratchet bits
idea: Adapt the escapement and pawl: a released 15 nm beam rests in one of four van der Waals detents along a serrated sidewall, is stepped by electrostatic pulses and read capacitively, with five sealed released layers stacked.
why: 10x at same cost: 2 bits per element x 5 deposited-and-released tiers; mechanical state needs no refresh and has no dielectric wearout.

title: Li-ion battery staging quantizes multi-level ionic storage
idea: Borrow graphite intercalation staging, where ions order into discrete stages with flat voltage plateaus: intercalate protons into few-layer MoS2/graphene hosts so each node rests on one of four stage plateaus read by open-circuit potential, in 3 stacked tiers.
why: 10x at same cost: plateau-quantized 2 bits/node robust to small self-discharge, x3 tiers, x~1.7 smaller node with no capacitor, ~10x.

title: LiDAR SPAD avalanche gain reads attofarad storage nodes
idea: Adapt single-photon avalanche diodes: store ~300 electrons on a 50 aF node and read by dumping them into a linear-mode avalanche junction (gain ~100) beside the bitline, so the cell is a 4F2 vertical transistor plus junction with no capacitor.
why: 10x at same cost: deleting the capacitor allows 4F2 at a tighter SAQP pitch (F ~8 nm) and two stacked tiers, ~10x bits per area without the EUV-heavy capacitor module.

title: Quanta-image-sensor jot stores each bit in twenty electrons
idea: Borrow Gigajot's pump-gate jot with ~0.2 e- rms read noise and ~400 uV/e- conversion gain: store a bit as 0 vs 20 electrons in a sub-aF buried node, read non-destructively by an in-cell source follower, and pack jots at 4F2 in stacked tiers.
why: 10x at same cost: ~20 e- instead of ~30,000 e- per bit shrinks the storage element ~1000x in charge, enabling 4F2 cells in 6 tiers, ~10x density.

title: Polarization-division multiplexing: charge plus polarization in one node
idea: Like fiber links sending two polarizations on one fiber, store two orthogonal variables per node: a low-field charge level and the polarization direction of a thin ferroelectric layer in the same stack, read first by low-field charge sensing, then by high-field switching-current sensing.
why: 10x at same cost: 2 bits per node x 5 vertical tiers, with both variables sharing one capacitor and one access device.

title: Jelly-roll memory: roll a display-fab sheet into dense cylinders
idea: Adapt cylindrical Li-ion jelly rolls: fabricate a large thin oxide-TFT gain-cell array on a strained release layer at display-fab cost per area, then self-roll it into 100-winding micro-cylinders whose edge lines contact a CMOS base die.
why: 10x at same cost: display fabs make area ~100x cheaper per m2 than DRAM wafers, so 100 windings of a 1/10-density sheet give ~10x bits per footprint at equal cost.

title: Type-II superlattice storage separates electrons from holes
idea: Adapt infrared-detector InAs/GaSb type-II superlattices (in Si/SiGe or oxide analogues): electrons and holes sit in spatially separated adjacent wells, so each site holds an independent electron bit and hole bit with recombination suppressed by the gap, in 5 tiers.
why: 10x at same cost: 2 bits per site x epitaxially defined tiers is ~10x per footprint; ambipolar read through separate n and p sense paths.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric 2D bilayers from solid-lubricant hBN
idea: Adapt hBN, sold as a solid lubricant because its layers slide: in AB/BA-stacked bilayers a one-row interlayer slide flips out-of-plane polarization, so 1 nm bilayers serve as storage films in 20 tiers read through 2D MoS2 channels.
why: 10x at same cost: a 1 nm storage film lets 20 tiers fit in a 3D-NAND-like stack, with fatigue-free sliding switching; ~10-15x bits per footprint.

title: Pipe-organ multimode nanomechanical parametron with many bits per membrane
idea: Like one organ wind chest feeding many pipes, a single 100 nm membrane has ~100 vibrational modes; pump each mode parametrically at twice its frequency from a shared comb so each mode holds a 0/pi phase bit, read by heterodyne detection.
why: 10x at same cost: ~100 bits per 100x100 nm element is ~100 nm2/bit (~9x), and phase states never leak; pump-comb energy is the risk.

title: UV-C LED AlGaN ultra-wide-bandgap capacitorless node in tiers
idea: Borrow AlGaN from UV-C LED fabs: a ~6 eV bandgap AlGaN channel transistor with near-zero leakage holds charge on its own gate node (no capacitor) for hours, enabling a 4F2 2T0C cell stacked in 8 low-temperature-deposited tiers.
why: 10x at same cost: no capacitor and no refresh, 1.5x from 4F2 x 8 tiers is ~12x; nitride tools are mature and present in the US.

title: Skyscraper sky-lobby bitlines enable 0.3 fF nodes in tall stacks
idea: Adapt sky lobbies, where express elevators stop at lobbies and local cars serve 16 floors: split each vertical bitline every 16 tiers with a local deposited-oxide sense amp, so each tier's node needs only ~0.3 fF against a short local bitline.
why: 10x at same cost: tiny capacitor-free nodes keep 128-tier stacks sensible; ~12x bits per footprint because the long-bitline capacitance problem is removed.

title: Nanopore-sequencer molecular tape with rewritable monomer charge
idea: Adapt Oxford Nanopore sequencing: a charged polymer shuttles back and forth through a solid-state nanopore; a write electrode oxidizes or reduces ferrocene side groups as they pass, and the pore current reads them back.
why: 10x at same cost: ~1 bit per nm of polymer coiled in a nanoreservoir; sequential like a racetrack but at molecular density, suited to warm-tier memory.

title: Silicon-on-Nothing cavity tiers from MEMS pressure sensors
idea: Borrow MEMS pressure-sensor empty-space-in-silicon: H2-anneal trench arrays so silicon migrates into sealed buried voids, repeat to form 20 single-crystal Si membranes separated by voids, then fill the voids with ALD high-k/TiN as plate capacitors under single-crystal lateral transistors.
why: 10x at same cost: single-crystal tiers without SiGe superlattice epitaxy remove the 3D lateral-transistor quality blocker (fact 2); 20 tiers at relaxed DUV pitch, ~10x.

title: Thermal-battery superionic gate freezes ions for perfect retention
idea: Adapt military thermal batteries whose electrolyte is solid (zero self-discharge) until heated: store the bit as Ag+ position in an Ag2S/AgI film that is superionic only above ~150 C; a ns Joule pulse unlocks the ion sublattice to write, and ions freeze in place on cooling.
why: 10x at same cost: a two-terminal element in a vertical 32-word-plane array sharing one hole litho, with no refresh; retention and write speed decoupled by the phase change.
